body: The year is 2000. The computers survived the millennium; the stock market has doubled in eighteen months; the outgoing President is from your party and the country is at peace. {leader} of {leader_state} means to keep it that way. Ahead lie fifty years nobody can see: wars, crashes, machines that think. The {party} Party will live through all of it, or not.

title: The computers held
sub: Y2K passes quietly. Markets open at records: the Nasdaq is up 86% in a year. The {party} Party holds the White House; the {rival_party} Party has its candidate in {rival}.

kicker: New Hampshire · three weeks to the primary
title: An insurgent in the snow
body: {challenger}, {challenger_office}, is running against you for the nomination on behalf of {weakest_name}, who say the party takes them for granted. A loss in New Hampshire would wound you. A long fight would wound the party.
advice: Their demand costs little with the other factions. Fighting is close to a coin toss.

choices.label: Adopt their demand: {weakest_demand_name}
choices.text: They stand down and endorse you. The pledge costs no Influence.

result.title: {challenger_last} endorses you
result.body: The {weakest_demand_name} goes into your platform. {weakest_name} are back on side.

choices.label: Fight them in New Hampshire
choices.text: Win and the challenge is over; lose and it drags into spring.

result.body_win: The challenge is over. The faction is not happy.
result.body_lose: The fight goes on to Super Tuesday, and it costs money and goodwill.

choices.label: Promise them a cabinet post
choices.text: A deal in a hotel room. They stand down; you owe them in 2001.

result.title: {challenger_last} stands down
result.body: {challenger} will expect a seat at the cabinet table.

title: The dot-com bubble
body: The Nasdaq has doubled in eighteen months on companies with no profits. The Fed chair wants political cover to lean against it before it pops.

lines.label: Chance the Nasdaq falls 30% or more
Growth in 2001 if it does, with no action
Growth in 2001 if it does, cooled now

choices.label: Back the Fed
choices.text: Slower growth now (−0.3 nationally); a softer landing when it comes.

choices.label: Let the boom run
choices.text: Nothing now. The forecast stands.

title: Tech slides; no panic
sub: The Nasdaq falls 24% from its March peak. Economists credit the Fed's early warning.

title: The bubble bursts
sub: The Nasdaq loses 37% in five weeks. Two trillion dollars of paper wealth, gone. Your party holds the White House, and owns the economy in November.

title: Who writes the platform?
body: The platform committee meets in a hotel ballroom with three hundred delegates and one draft. How much of it is yours?

choices.label: Write it yourself
choices.text: +12 Influence to spend on pledges. The factions grumble (−3 each).

choices.label: Let the factions write it
choices.text: Every allied faction +8 friendship.

choices.label: Keep it short and vague
choices.text: +2 Momentum. Nobody is offended; nobody is inspired.

title: Choose a running mate
body: The running mate joins the board as a unit: a second candidate who rallies twice as hard in their home state. What they hide you find out by vetting, or in October.

title: The nomination is yours
body: Twenty thousand delegates, a week of speeches, and a party that fought you through the primaries. Tonight you accept its nomination. The speech sets the tone for the fall.

choices.label: Hope: one country, one future
choices.text: Broad and warm: +1.0 nationally, +2 Momentum.

choices.label: Fight: name what is wrong
choices.text: Your factions love it (+10 each); swing voters less so (+0.2 nationally).

choices.label: The plan for day one
choices.text: Dry, but it reads well: +0.6 nationally, +8 Ideas.

title: Nine weeks to go
sub: From now on, each turn is two weeks. Every rally, every ad and every faction counts double the attention.

title: The {third_name} is on the ballot
body: {third_name}, the party of {third_faction} voters you lost, is polling {third_share}% in its strongest states. Every vote it wins there could have been yours.

choices.label: Court their voters
choices.text: {third_faction} +15 friendship; if they come back, the third party fades.

choices.label: Attack them as spoilers
choices.text: Their share falls by a third; their voters remember (−5).

choices.label: Ignore them
choices.text: Spend nothing on it.

kicker: Boston · the first debate · 46 million watching
title: The first debate
body: {rival} has spent a week at debate camp. Your team has three plans for the night. The odds come from your ratings.

choices.label: Go deep on the plan
choices.text: A policy night. Big if it works; dull if not.

choices.label: Land the line
choices.text: One sentence that leads every newscast.

choices.label: Stay steady
choices.text: No mistakes, no headlines.

title: The story about {mate}
body: Business records: a consulting firm, a foreign client, fees nobody disclosed. The story runs at six.

choices.label: Stand by {mate_first}
choices.text: Loyal. The story runs for a week.

choices.label: Release everything tonight
choices.text: A gamble that the details are dull.

choices.label: Prove it is a fake
choices.text: Your forensics team says the key document was generated.

title: An old arrest record
body: A local reporter has a 1976 arrest record: you, twenty-two, a traffic stop, a night in a county jail. It is true, and it is five days from the debate prep you needed.

choices.label: Confirm it and apologise
choices.text: Honest and quick: −0.4 nationally.

choices.label: Attack the timing and the source
choices.text: If it works, the story becomes their dirty trick.

result.lose: It became a week of stories

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: Let it burn out: −0.8 nationally.

title: The last word
body: One more speech, run on every channel for the last week. Choose how you want to be remembered.

choices.label: Optimism
choices.text: +0.6 nationally, +3 Momentum.

choices.label: Contrast
choices.text: +0.4 nationally; their momentum stalls.

choices.label: Fear
choices.text: +1.0 nationally, unless it backfires.

title: President {leader_last}
sub: The {party} Party holds the White House with {ev_you} electoral votes, {senate} senators and {house} representatives. The map stays on the table: now you govern it.

title: President {rival_last}
sub: The {rival_party} Party takes the White House. Your party holds {senate} Senate seats and {house} in the House. The 2002 midterms start now.

title: Form your cabinet
body: Cabinet secretaries are your great people in office: their ratings shape their departments for years. A unity pick from outside your coalition wins approval and costs your factions.

title: The lights go out in California
body: Rolling blackouts across the state; wholesale power prices up tenfold since last spring; traders gaming a market nobody fully understood. The governor wants federal price caps.

choices.label: Impose federal price caps
choices.text: The blackouts ease; the free-market wing is furious.

choices.label: Investigate the traders
choices.text: Slow, popular, and right: +1.5 in California; it takes a year.

choices.label: Let the market sort it out
choices.text: The base cheers; California does not.

title: What to do with the surplus
body: The budget office projects $5.6 trillion of surpluses over ten years. Every faction has a plan for it. Your first law sets the tone.

choices.label: Cut taxes across the board
choices.text: The Tax Cut becomes your first law, with a head start.

choices.label: A drug benefit for seniors
choices.text: The Medicare Drug Benefit becomes your first law, with a head start.

choices.label: Pay down the debt
choices.text: No law yet. Approval +2; the factions shrug.

title: A warning on the desk
body: The counter-terrorism chief has been trying to get this in front of the new administration since the transition: a terrorist network is planning a major attack inside the United States. History has it on the calendar for September. History is a default, not a law.

lines.label: Chance of a major attack on U.S. soil

advice: Cheap measures taken early are worth more than expensive ones taken late. The Aviation Security Act is on the White House's list of laws.

choices.label: Convene the principals this week
choices.text: Make it the first priority: −12 points on the forecast.

choices.label: Ask for a fuller report
choices.text: Prudent, and slow.

choices.label: Demand hearings
choices.text: In opposition, all you can do is make noise: −6 on the forecast; accused of politicising intelligence (−0.2).

choices.label: Keep it quiet
choices.text: Do not use intelligence for politics.

title: A spy plane down in China
body: A U.S. Navy surveillance plane has collided with a Chinese fighter over the South China Sea. The Chinese pilot is missing; the damaged plane landed on Hainan Island, and its twenty-four crew are being held.

choices.label: Express regret, carefully worded
choices.text: The crew come home in eleven days; hawks call it an apology.

choices.label: Demand the crew back, no apology
choices.text: Firm. It works fast or it does not.

result.win: The crew are home in a week

choices.label: Back the President, quietly
choices.text: Politics stops at the water's edge: +2 Momentum.

choices.label: Call it a humiliation
choices.text: Hawks love it (+10); swing voters wince (−0.2).

title: "Determined to strike"
body: The daily brief carries a warning in its title: the network is determined to strike inside the United States. Field offices have flagged men at flight schools. The forecast stands at {threat}%.

choices.label: Order a summer surge
choices.text: Airports, visas, the flight-school leads: −15 on the forecast, −1 approval.

choices.label: Make the agencies share what they have
choices.text: FBI and CIA in one room: −8 on the forecast.

choices.label: Note it and move on
choices.text: It is August.

choices.label: Go public with the warnings
choices.text: −5 on the forecast; −0.3 nationally for alarmism.

choices.label: Stay silent
choices.text: Nothing changes.

title: Attack on America
sub: Hijacked airliners strike the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; a fourth crashes in Pennsylvania. Nearly three thousand people are killed. The country rallies to its President.

title: Plot foiled
sub: Nineteen men are in custody after a coordinated sweep of flight schools and airports. Most Americans will never know how close it came; the people who stopped it do.

title: The end of the beginning
body: Two years in. {year_end_line} The 2002 midterms are eleven months away, and the century has forty-seven years to go.

choices.label: Close the year
choices.text: See the record, and what comes next.
